title: Fund control can exist in two countries
full_text:
The central management and control (CMC) of an SMSF will be viewed as remaining in Australia even when trustees live overseas, but key criteria must be met by each of them, DBA Lawyers director Shaun Backhaus has pointed out.
Backhaus said while taxation law requires the CMC of an SMSF to ‘ordinarily’ be in Australia, it can also be in two places based on the number of trustees here and overseas, and their involvement in the fund’s management.
To illustrate this, he gave the example of April and May, who are directors of a corporate trustee, and April permanently moves to Singapore while May stays in Australia.
The pair continue to hold twice-yearly meetings to discuss the fund’s investment strategy and pass resolutions and minutes, and use email throughout the year to discuss asset purchase decisions and inform their accountant and financial planner in Australia of actions to take on their behalf.
“All their advice is given from Australia and the fund holds Australian equities and real estate, so where is the CMC of this fund?” Backhaus said in a recent webinar.
“You can have the CMC in multiple places, according to an ATO [taxation] ruling [2008/9].
“That ruling says when you have an equal number of individual trustees or directors, both in Australia and overseas, and everyone is substantially and actively participating in the CMC of the fund, the CMC will ordinarily be in Australia and it will also ordinarily be overseas. It’s in both places.
“On those facts, we had April and May both actively participating in the central management and control of the fund, so it’s ordinarily in Australia and Singapore.”
He noted this was useful for SMSF trustees who intend to travel and spend an extended period away.
“When people are going overseas, often the fund is looking to have them resign and put someone in their place with an enduring power of attorney, which can be done,” he said.
“It’s also worth keeping in mind you can have them stay in the fund when it’s equal people in Australia and outside and they can still be involved in the fund and the CMC will still be viewed as ordinarily in Australia.”
